entities.name: William de Bohun, 1st Earl of Northampton
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
William de Bohun, 1st Earl of Northampton, was a powerful English nobleman and military commander who played a crucial role in the Second Barons' War (1264-1267). Born into the powerful Bohun family, William de Bohun married Maud de Braose, daughter of the powerful Lord Rhys ap Gruffydd of Glamorgan, and thus secured significant alliances with the Welsh nobility. Through his military campaigns and strategic marriages, William de Bohun expanded the Bohun family's territories and influence, earning him a prominent place in the history of medieval England. He died on September 24, 1360, at the age of approximately 80, leaving behind a legacy of military prowess, diplomatic skill, and a lasting impact on the English nobility.

The Second Barons' War, in which William de Bohun played a key role, was a pivotal conflict that shaped the course of English history. The war, sparked by tensions between King Henry III and the rebellious barons, saw the rise of the powerful Bohun family and their strategic alliances with the Welsh nobility.

William de Bohun's military campaigns and diplomatic efforts had a lasting impact on the region. His strategic marriages and alliances with the Welsh nobility helped to secure English control over the region, paving the way for future English expansion. His military prowess and leadership skills also earned him a reputation as one of the most skilled and feared commanders of his time.

The Bohun family's influence continued to shape English history long after William de Bohun's death. His descendants went on to play prominent roles in English politics and society, including the notable Earl of Northampton, Thomas de Bohun, who served as Lord Lieutenant of Ireland.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, William de Bohun's name remains synonymous with military prowess and diplomatic skill, earning him a place among the most notable figures in English history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: William de Bohun's life and legacy have been immortalized in various historical accounts, including the chronicles of the time, which describe him as a 'great and powerful lord' who 'commanded the greatest and most numerous army in England'. His military campaigns and diplomatic efforts secured English control over the region, paving the way for future English expansion.
